IK_EN_109.publisher: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (EN, abridged) 109: no Makki/Madani verdict in this abridgement; Muslim (Jabir) tawaf 2 rak'ahs; Muslim (Abu Hurayra) Fajr sunnah; Ahmad (Ibn 'Umar) Fajr + Maghrib; quarter of Quran mentioned; offer 'it has been said' (worship our idols a year, we worship yours a year), no chain; repetition: first = objects of worship, second = manner of worship (ma masdariyya); Bukhari: lakum dinukum = kufr, wa liya din = Islam; cf. 10:41, 28:55; name 'Surat Qul ya Ayyuhal-Kafirun'

TB_109.publisher: Tafsir al-Tabari (AR) 109: (a) Muhammad bin Musa al-Harashi - Abu Khalaf - Dawud - 'Ikrima - Ibn 'Abbas: wealth/marriage offer, else Lat and 'Uzza a year / your God a year; (b) Ya'qub - Ibn 'Ulayya - Ibn Ishaq - Sa'id bin Mina mawla al-Bakhtari: al-Walid bin al-Mughira, al-'As bin Wa'il, al-Aswad bin al-Muttalib, Umayya bin Khalaf proposed mutual worship; Tabari's own explanation: surah addresses specific mushrikeen, cuts off their hope of compromise; negation covers present, future and past; grammarians: repetition = emphasis (cf. 94:5-6); verse 6: their religion is theirs and his is his, he will never leave it; no Makki/Madani statement

QT_109.publisher: Tafsir al-Qurtubi (AR) 109:1: Makki per Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan, 'Ikrima; Madani per one of two views of Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, al-Dahhak; 6 ayat; nickname al-Muqashqishatan (with al-Ikhlas; al-Asma'i: cleanse from nifaq); virtues incl. third/quarter (Anas, al-Anbari), Farwa bin Nawfal before sleep, Jubayr bin Mut'im travel, Ibn 'Abbas 'most hateful to Iblis'; occasion: Ibn Ishaq etc. from Ibn 'Abbas (four leaders), Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas (touch idols), wealth/marriage version; al-Mawardi: reply to a specific group; repetition: emphasis (most), repeated requests, different times (al-Akhfash, al-Mubarrad), ma masdariyya

QT_109_6.publisher: Tafsir al-Qurtubi (AR) 109:6: sense of threat (cf. 28:55); 'qila' abrogated by the sword verse / whole surah abrogated / not abrogated as it is khabar; din = recompense (alternative)

MQ_109.publisher: Ma'ariful Qur'an (EN) 109: offers (Ibn Ishaq via Ibn 'Abbas in Qurtubi; Tabarani via Ibn 'Abbas in Mazhari; Abu Salih) possibly at different times - surah ends compromise once and for all; repetition: Bukhari = present vs future; Ibn Kathir = objects vs manner; others = emphasis (Ibn Kathir/Ibn Jarir); verse 6 neither guarantees nor permits disbelief; Islam values tolerance, kindness, politeness, peace in human dealings but no compromise in tenets; treaties (8:61) allowed; majority: not abrogated; before-sleep hadith (Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud); Mazhari reports (Jubayr, scorpion) not used

facts.claim: Arabic 109:1-6 = Tanzil Uthmani v1.1 bytes (ayat[]); CC BY 3.0, verbatim, credit Tanzil Project + link; sha256 on PC

Hindi = SARAL BHAAVARTH from accepted translations (Suhel Farooq Khan, Muhammad Farooq Khan, Mahmud al-Hasan PD; English check Sahih International, Hilali-Khan); nothing copied; '(ai rasool)' and Hilali's bracket additions not taken
Latin transliteration for the Devanagari ucharan (Tanzil ara-quran-la + quran411 ara-quran-la1); ucharan.md rows U1-U6
Name al-Kafirun (الكافرون = those who deny/disbelieve), taken from the word in ayah 1; surah 109 in the mushaf; 6 ayat; juz 30

Makki per majority (Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan, 'Ikrima; Ibn 'Atiyya and Ibn Kathir 'by agreement'; quran.com 'by consensus'; Tanzil Meccan); Madani reported from Ibn al-Zubayr, and one of two views of Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, al-Dahhak
Order of revelation 18 (after al-Ma'un, before al-Fil) in the standard list used by Tanzil/quran.com, also given by Ibn 'Ashur
facts.grade: maana hua (ek mash'hoor fehrist ke mutabiq)

facts.claim: Other names: 'Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun' (al-Bukhari's title; Ibn Kathir); al-Muqashqisha (shared with al-Ikhlas; Qurtubi, Ibn 'Ashur citing al-Kashshaf/al-Itqan); Surat al-'Ibada and Surat al-Din (Ibn 'Ashur + quran.com)
Main message: clear and final separation in worship/belief between tawhid and shirk; no give-and-take in worship
Background (tafseer-level, not one narration): Makka's mushrik leaders hoped for / repeatedly sought a compromise with the Prophet in worship; the surah was revealed to end that hope finally
The surah answers a specific group of Makka's mushrikeen of that time (not a label for every non-Muslim)

Narrated offer 'you worship our gods a year, we worship your God a year' (Tabari: Ibn 'Abbas via Abu Khalaf; Ibn Ishaq from Sa'id bin Mina; al-Wahidi; Wahb) - each chain weak or mursal (Abu Khalaf 'Abdullah bin 'Isa weak per Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari 8/333; Sa'id bin Mina a tabi'i = mursal)
facts.grade: chhoda gaya (sanad kamzor) - mash'hoor, sab badi tafseeron me

facts.claim: The Prophet recited al-Kafirun and al-Ikhlas in the two sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr (Muslim 726; Abu Dawud 1256 sahih)
He recited al-Ikhlas and al-Kafirun in the two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim after tawaf (Muslim 1218a)
Recite al-Kafirun before sleep: it is a declaration of freedom (bara'at) from shirk (Abu Dawud 5055, Tirmidhi 3403)
Also in the 2 rak'ahs after Maghrib (Tirmidhi 431, Ibn Mas'ud) / Fajr a month (Tirmidhi 417, Ibn 'Umar)
facts.grade: ikhtilaaf (grade: Shakir/al-Albani sahih or hasan sahih, Zubair Ali Zai da'if) - video optional, safer skip

facts.claim: 'Equal to a quarter of the Quran' (Tirmidhi 2893/2894/2895)
109:1 - 'Say: O you who deny/disbelieve' - Allah tells the Prophet to address them
109:2 - I do not worship what you worship
109:3 - nor are you worshippers of the One I worship
109:4 - nor will I be a worshipper of what you have worshipped
109:5 - nor will you be worshippers of the One I worship
109:6 - for you your religion (din/way), for me mine
'Qul' = the reply is a command from Allah, not the Prophet's own offer; the address is to that group

Why 2-5 repeat: (a) emphasis to cut off all hope (Qurtubi: most scholars; Tabari reports grammarians; Ma'ariful); (b) different times - now vs future/past (al-Bukhari per Ma'ariful; Tabari; Qurtubi: al-Akhfash, al-Mubarrad); (c) what is worshipped vs how worship is done (Ibn Kathir; Qurtubi 'ma masdariyya'; Ma'ariful)
facts.grade: ikhtilaaf (teen maane hue qaul, koi takraav nahi)

facts.claim: 109:6 = clear separation in worship/belief; it is NOT approval of shirk / not 'all religions are the same' (al-Bukhari via Ibn Kathir: lakum dinukum = kufr, wa liya din = Islam; Ma'ariful: neither permits nor guarantees disbelief; Tafheem: not tolerance in matters of faith; Qurtubi: carries a warning, cf. 28:55)
The separation is in worship/belief only; kindness, fair dealing, good relations and treaties with non-Muslims who do not fight remain (Ma'ariful on 109:6; Quran 60:8 with Ibn Kathir; Bukhari 2620)
Abrogation of 109:6 (sword verse) - Qurtubi/Zad al-Masir 'qila' vs Ma'ariful 'majority: not abrogated'; din = recompense (Qurtubi alternative; Thanawi per Ma'ariful)
